> ## Verified status
>
> - Tata Steel repeatedly describes a **~1 MTPA HIsarna demonstration plant at Jamshedpur** as planned, proposed, being worked toward or to be set up.
> - The report states that the **Board has approved a 1 MTPA HIsarna demonstration plant in India**.
> - It also says the company is progressing engineering, permitting/regulatory work and validation, rather than reporting EPC completion, construction start, commissioning or operation.
> - The existing IJmuiden pilot is described as having operated for over a decade; this is the pilot evidence base, not the status of the future Jamshedpur unit.
>
> ## Technical scope
>
> - HIsarna combines a high-temperature melting cyclone with a smelting vessel.
> - The company says the route directly uses iron-ore fines and powdered coal, eliminating coke ovens and sinter plants.
> - The report describes relevance to lower-grade Indian ores and a concentrated off-gas suitable for carbon capture.
> - It records prior trials with Indian raw materials but does not disclose the Jamshedpur demonstration's detailed feed blend or operating data.
>
> ## Interpretation boundary
>
> - Board approval and engineering/regulatory activity are stronger than a general corporate aspiration, but they are not evidence of FID, EPC award, site mobilisation or groundbreaking.
> - The 1 MTPA figure is a demonstration design target, not achieved annual production.
> - Marketing language such as “proven pilot” and emissions claims must remain company-attributed unless independently measured operating data is available.
